Automatically determine optimal PCA dimensions using multiple robust methods

Source: R/11c-FindRobustElbow.R
FindRobustElbow.Rd

This function combines multiple statistical approaches to automatically determine the optimal number of principal components (PCs) for downstream single-cell analysis. It integrates variance-based heuristics, elbow detection algorithms, and provides comprehensive visualization for result validation.

Usage

FindRobustElbow(
  obj,
  verbose = SigBridgeRUtils::getFuncOption("verbose") %||% TRUE,
  ndims = 50L
)

Arguments

obj

A Seurat object that has PCA computed (after RunPCA) or a numeric matrix of cell embeddings (cells x PCs).

verbose

Logical, if TRUE outputs detailed method results and creates visualization plot. If FALSE returns only the final dimension.

ndims

Integer, maximum number of dimensions to consider (default: 50L). Values exceeding the number of PCs stored in the "pca" reduction are capped at the available number of PCs.

Value

Integer, the recommended number of PCA dimensions for downstream analysis

Details

The numerical work is delegated to the C++ routine find_robust_elbow_cpp(), which receives the PCA cell embeddings as an S4-aware matrix view created by beachmat::initializeCpp(). Columns are streamed through tatami (see Rtatami.h), so the embeddings are never coerced into a dense base matrix and only the requested ndims columns are touched. For each of those PCs the routine computes the standard deviation, the explained variance, the percentage of explained variance, and the cumulative percentage, which are then fed into the six heuristics described below.

The recommended dimension is the second largest value among the following candidates:

  • cumulative variance above 90\

  • cumulative variance above 80\

  • last PC explaining more variance than the mean;

  • last PC explaining more than two standard deviations of the variance;

  • maximum second derivative of the variance curve;

  • largest distance between the variance curve and the chord joining the first and the last PC;

  • the fixed anchors 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35.

The fixed anchors are independent of the data, so the raw recommendation can exceed the number of PCs that were actually computed. The final value is therefore capped at the number of available PCs (i.e. ndims).

When verbose = TRUE and the session is interactive, the per-method candidates are plotted on top of the variance curve by the internal helper plot_robust_elbow().

See also

Other single_cell_preprocess: FilterTumorCell(), Pattern2Colname(), QCPatternDetect(), RegisterSeuratMethod(), SCAnnotate(), SCIntegrate(), SCPreProcess(), SCPreProcessStrategy

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# After running PCA on Seurat object
pbmc <- RunPCA(pbmc, npcs = 50)
optimal_dims <- FindRobustElbow(pbmc, verbose = TRUE)
pbmc <- FindNeighbors(pbmc, dims = 1:optimal_dims)
} # }
